documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT

Ms. Pratt is a 70-year-old retired grade-school teacher transferring care after her previous internist closed his panel. Brought a bag of bottles, which we went through together.

HPI: Hypertension for many years, on lisinopril alone, home readings she says are usually in the 130s. Type 2 diabetes about a decade, metformin 1000 twice a day, no hypoglycemia, no polyuria. High cholesterol on simvastatin 20 at night. Baby aspirin daily, started by her old doctor. Feels well. No chest pain, no shortness of breath, no foot numbness, no vision change since her cataract surgeries.

PMH: HTN, T2DM, hyperlipidemia.
PSH: TAH at 45. Cataract extraction with lens implants, both eyes.
Meds: lisinopril 10 daily, metformin 1000 BID, simvastatin 20 qhs, aspirin 81 daily.
Allergies: none to medications.
Family: mother developed Alzheimer's in her mid-70s. Father had type 2 diabetes and an MI at 68. Both parents hypertensive.
Social: lives alone in Amherst, drives, active in her church book group. Never smoked. A glass of wine once or twice a month.

Exam: Pleasant, well appearing. Vitals as recorded. Fundi not well seen through undilated pupils; lens implants noted. Neck supple, no bruits. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Feet: pulses 2+, monofilament intact bilaterally, no calluses or ulcers. No edema.

Assessment/Plan:
1. Hypertension - at goal today on lisinopril 10. Continue.
2. Type 2 diabetes - A1c, CMP, urine microalbumin today. Continue metformin. Eye exam with her optometrist yearly; she will have the report sent.
3. Hyperlipidemia - lipids today, simvastatin 20.
4. Aspirin - continue for now.
5. Health maintenance - hep C antibody once. Requesting old records for colonoscopy, mammogram and vaccine dates. Flu shot next month when high-dose arrives.

Follow up 3 months.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Ms. Pratt, your labs from Tuesday look good. A1c is 6.5, nicely controlled. Kidney function and potassium normal, no protein in the urine, and the hepatitis C screen is negative. Cholesterol numbers are reasonable on the simvastatin. No changes. See you in December.

documents.title: Office Visit - headaches
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: on-and-off headaches and lightheadedness x about 2 months.

HPI: 72 yo with HTN, T2DM, HLD. Over the last couple of months she gets a dull frontal ache a few afternoons a week, sometimes with a brief woozy feeling when she stands from the couch. No vertigo, no falls, no visual loss, no weakness or numbness, no jaw pain. Has not been checking pressures at home since her cuff broke. Taking lisinopril daily.

Meds: lisinopril 10, metformin 1000 BID, simvastatin 20 qhs, ASA 81.

Exam: BP 162/78 (repeat similar), HR 78, BMI 29. Fundoscopic: no AV nicking, hemorrhages or exudates - no hypertensive retinopathy. Neck: no bruits. CV: regular, a soft 2/6 systolic ejection murmur at the upper sternal border, otherwise normal. Lungs clear. Neuro grossly nonfocal. No edema.

Fasting labs drawn today: glucose 138, A1c 7.2, total chol 190, LDL 100, HDL 45, creatinine 1.0, eGFR 60.

A/P:
1. Essential hypertension, above goal on lisinopril alone, likely behind the headaches. Adding hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg each morning. BMP in 2-3 weeks. New home cuff - bring readings.
2. T2DM - A1c 7.2, acceptable. Continue metformin.
3. HLD - LDL 100 on simvastatin 20. Continue.
4. Murmur - soft, noted today.
Recheck 3 months, sooner if headaches worsen or any neuro symptoms.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
First in-person visit since February. Mask on, screened at door.

S: Six months since we added HCTZ. Headaches resolved. Now complains of feeling washed out most days, and up 3 times a night to void, which is new for her. No dysuria. No chest pain, palpitations or ankle swelling. No polydipsia that she notices.

O: BP 138/86, HR 78. Mucous membranes moist, looks well hydrated. Heart regular with the same soft systolic ejection murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P:
1. Fatigue and nocturia on HCTZ - labs drawn this morning; will call with results.
2. HTN - better controlled.
3. Lipids due - drawn.

ADDENDUM 16:40: Labs back. Na 132, K 3.2, Cl 98, CO2 24, BUN 18, Cr 1.0, fasting glucose 126, Ca 10.6, Mg 1.6, uric acid 8.5. Total cholesterol 210, LDL 140, TG 200. This is a thiazide picture - low sodium, low potassium and magnesium, high calcium and uric acid - and fits her fatigue and nocturia. Stopping hydrochlorothiazide; added to her intolerance list. Potassium chloride 20 mEq daily x 7 days. Repeat BMP and Mg in 2 weeks. Continue lisinopril 10. Called pt and explained; she has an old bottle of HCTZ and will set it aside. LDL up from 100; continue simvastatin 20 for now.

documents.title: Medication change
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Ms. Pratt, as we discussed by phone: STOP hydrochlorothiazide (the morning water pill). START potassium chloride 20 mEq, one a day with food for 7 days only - it was sent to your pharmacy. Keep taking lisinopril, metformin, simvastatin and aspirin as usual. Blood work again on September 1. Please keep a few blood pressure readings for me.

documents.title: RE: Medication change
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Got it. The potassium pills are big but I will manage. I put the old water pills in a bag for the pharmacy take-back. Jean

documents.title: Electrolytes normalized

documents.title: Office Visit - memory
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Visit requested by daughter, who came with her.

HPI: Daughter has noticed over roughly the past year that her mother loses track of things - keys, glasses, the checkbook - misses appointments she would never have missed before, and asks the same question two or three times in one phone call without remembering the answer. Earlier this year she got lost driving back from the grocery store and arrived home after dark; she gave up driving on her own after that. Pt herself says her memory is 'what you'd expect at my age' but agrees she stopped driving. No falls, no hallucinations, no change in gait, no urinary accidents, no head injury. Mood okay.

Family: mother had Alzheimer's starting in her mid-70s.

Exam: pleasant, cooperative, well groomed. Vitals as charted. Brief screen: misses delayed recall of items, clock drawing slightly off. Neuro: nonfocal, gait normal.

A/P: Progressive short-term memory loss over a year, functional change (stopped driving), strong family history. Referring to neurology for formal evaluation. Meds reviewed - nothing sedating. Daughter will start checking her pill box weekly. Pt agreeable.

conditions.label: Alzheimer disease
conditions.note: probable, by clinical criteria and imaging

reports.text:
Indication: progressive memory loss.
Technique: axial noncontrast CT of the head.
Findings: Generalized prominence of the sulci and ventricles consistent with diffuse cerebral volume loss. No acute hemorrhage. No territorial infarct. No mass, mass effect or midline shift. No extra-axial collection. Basal cisterns patent. Calvarium intact.
reports.conclusion: Generalized cerebral atrophy. No evidence of stroke or mass lesion.

documents.title: Neurology Consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT NEUROLOGY - CONSULTATION
Date of service: 08/17/2021
Referred by: primary care, for memory loss

Thank you for referring Mrs. Jean Pratt, a 74-year-old right-handed retired teacher, seen today with her daughter.

History: For about a year her daughter has watched her become more forgetful: items are misplaced daily, appointments slip by, and she repeats questions and cannot bring back conversations from the day before. She still lives by herself and handles her own bathing, dressing and meals. Some months ago she became lost driving home and has not driven since. No hallucinations, no tremor, no falls.

PMH: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia. Hysterectomy; bilateral cataract surgery.
Medications (per referral list): metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, simvastatin 20 mg qhs, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: mother with Alzheimer's from age 75; father diabetes, MI at 68; parental hypertension.
Social: never smoker, occasional wine.

Exam: Alert. Oriented to self and place; not to the date. MMSE 20/30, points lost on orientation, three-word recall and serial subtraction. Language fluent. Cranial nerves intact. Normal strength, tone and reflexes. Gait normal, no focal deficits.

Data: Na 140, K 4.2, Cl 102, HCO3 24, BUN 18, Cr 0.9, glucose 98, TSH 2.5, B12 400. Noncontrast CT head today: generalized atrophy without infarct or mass.

Impression: Progressive amnestic cognitive decline with functional impact and a normal reversible-cause screen, most consistent with Alzheimer's disease (probable).

Recommendations: discussed the diagnosis with the patient and daughter. Safety review - agree she should not drive. Daughter to look into help with finances and medications. Follow up here in 6 months.

Neurology

Indication: Alzheimer disease, follow-up.

OUTPATIENT NEUROLOGY - FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 02/18/2022

Mrs. Pratt returns with her daughter six months after her initial cognitive evaluation of August 2021.

Interval: Recent events slip away more - appointments, what was said on the phone. She misplaces things more often than in the summer and now pauses mid-sentence hunting for words. Still lives alone and still pays her own bills. Not driving.

Medications per list: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 10, hydrochlorothiazide 25, simvastatin 20, aspirin 81. NKDA.

Exam: Alert, oriented to person and place, not to date. MMSE 24/30 (lost points: orientation, recall, serial 7s). Speech fluent with intact comprehension and repetition. No focal findings.

Imaging: repeat noncontrast head CT today shows generalized atrophy, most marked in the medial temporal lobes and hippocampi.

Impression: Alzheimer disease. Score today a little higher than in August, within the range of session-to-session variation; history indicates continued slow progression. Imaging pattern supports the diagnosis.

Plan: supervision of finances discussed with daughter. Return in 6 months.

OUTPATIENT NEUROLOGY
Date of service: 08/29/2022

Mrs. Pratt, 75, with Alzheimer disease first evaluated in this clinic 07/2021 [sic, 08/2021] and again 02/2022, comes with her daughter for scheduled reassessment; I am seeing her for the first time, taking over from my colleague.

Daughter's account: across the past year her mother loses the thread of conversations, mislays things constantly and can no longer keep her accounts straight - the daughter has taken over the checkbook. Before she gave up the car she had become lost more than once on routes she had driven for decades. She lives alone and still sets out her own pills from the blister packs.

Meds as listed by referral: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 10, hydrochlorothiazide 25, simvastatin 20, aspirin 81. NKDA.

Exam: BP 140/85. Neatly dressed and groomed. Mildly disoriented to time. Recalls 0 of 3 words at 5 minutes; serial 7s labored. MMSE 22/30. Motor and sensory exam nonfocal.

Labs today: fasting glucose 160. CBC, electrolytes, renal function and TSH normal.

Assessment: Alzheimer disease with gradual progression; now needs help with finances.
Plan: daughter to increase daily check-ins. Home safety reviewed. Return 1 year, sooner if behavior changes. Fasting glucose forwarded to PCP.

documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT NEUROLOGY
Date of service: 08/16/2023

Annual reassessment of Alzheimer disease, first evaluated here 08/2021. Her daughter attends.

Interval: attention has slipped further; bills are beyond her and she asks the same things over and over. Several times this spring she left a burner on, and once she could not find her way back from a neighbor's house a few doors down. The family describes her as quieter and more withdrawn, at times short-tempered, and she loses the thread of group conversation. No seizures, no hallucinations, no sudden step-downs.

Meds per list: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 10, hydrochlorothiazide 25, simvastatin 20, aspirin 81. NKDA.
Social: never smoker; no alcohol.

Exam: disoriented to time and place. Recalls none of three words after a delay. Clock drawing disorganized. Strength, sensation and coordination intact.

Labs: B12 and thyroid function normal.

Assessment: Alzheimer disease, progressive, now with safety issues at home.
Plan: stove shut-off device and supervision recommended; family considering more help at home. Follow up as needed or in 1 year.

Neurology

conditions.label: Major depressive disorder, single episode, severe with psychotic features

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Visit 02/25/2025, received by fax 03/03/2025

CC: depression, hearing voices, not eating.

HPI: 77-year-old woman with Alzheimer disease, progressive over roughly five years and followed by neurology, brought by her daughter. For six weeks she has been severely depressed - hopeless, guilty, no interest in anything she used to enjoy. She hears voices calling her worthless and telling her not to eat, and for two weeks has refused nearly all food and drink. Daughter estimates 5 kg lost. Recently started on sertraline by her PCP.

PMH: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia, Alzheimer disease, prior thiazide reaction.
Home meds per daughter's list and old record: metformin, lisinopril, sertraline 25; hydrochlorothiazide 25, simvastatin 20, aspirin 81.
Allergies: NKDA on our record.
Social: never smoker, occasional alcohol (old record), retired teacher.
Family: mother Alzheimer's; father diabetes, MI.

Exam: BP 130/85, P 78, BMI 22. Lethargic, oriented to person, place and time. Thin. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Nonfocal.

Labs: Na 142, K 4.1, Cl 100, HCO3 24, BUN 21, Cr 1.0, glucose 160 (fasting), A1c 7.2, TSH 2.5.

ED course: oral fluids encouraged and taken with coaxing. Psychiatry consulted.

Diagnosis: major depressive disorder, single episode, severe, with psychotic features.
Disposition: admitted to inpatient geriatric psychiatry, voluntary with daughter as proxy in agreement.

Emergency Medicine

medications.reason: major depressive disorder with psychotic features

documents.title: Geriatric Psychiatry Discharge Summary
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
INPATIENT GERIATRIC PSYCHIATRY - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 02/25/2025 via ED. Discharged 03/07/2025.

Admission diagnosis: major depressive disorder, single episode, severe with psychotic features. Comorbid Alzheimer disease, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia.

Course: Arrived withdrawn, accepting only sips. With 1:1 feeding support at meals and close nursing observation she began eating and drinking within the first week. Sertraline, started outpatient at 25 mg, was increased to 50 mg daily on day 2 and tolerated. The derogatory voices became less frequent and by discharge she no longer reported them. Mood brighter, engaging with staff, sleeping at night. No falls, no behavioral emergencies. Discharge weight 56 kg.

Discharge medications: sertraline 50 mg daily; metformin 1000 mg BID; lisinopril 10 mg daily; simvastatin 20 mg nightly; aspirin 81 mg daily.

Disposition: home to her daughter's house, where she will now live; daughter will manage medications and meals.

Follow-up: PCP within one week. Return to ED for refusal of food or fluids or return of voices.

Geriatric Psychiatry

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Arrived 02/27/2026 16:20, discharged 02/28/2026 10:30. Received 03/02/2026.

CC: two days of worsening confusion and agitation.

HPI: 78-year-old woman with progressive Alzheimer disease and a 2025 ED presentation for depression with psychosis, brought in by family. Over two days she has become more confused and agitated - shouting at relatives and twice shoving the daughter who cares for her. Family reports no falls, no head injury and no new medications.

PMH: Alzheimer disease, MDD with psychotic features (2025), hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia.
Home meds (from our prior record): metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 10, hydrochlorothiazide 25, simvastatin 20, aspirin 81.
Allergies: NKDA. Social: never smoker, occasional alcohol per old record.

Exam: T 37.2 C, BP 150/85, P 88, RR 16. Alert but disoriented to time and place. Cannot follow multistep commands, easily distracted. Speech coherent but drifts between topics. Nonfocal neuro exam. Heart regular, lungs clear, abdomen soft.

Results: Na 140, K 4.2, Cl 102, HCO3 24, BUN 18, Cr 0.9, glucose 98, Ca 9.2. CBC, LFTs and TSH within normal limits. Urinalysis unremarkable. Portable CXR: no acute disease.

Course: quiet room, family at bedside, lights down overnight. No sedatives given. By morning calmer, eating breakfast, at her baseline per daughter.

Diagnosis: delirium due to a medical condition, superimposed on Alzheimer disease; no precipitant identified on workup.
Disposition: discharged home with family. PCP follow-up within the week.

Emergency Medicine

documents.title: Post-ED Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ED record reviewed: 2/27-2/28, delirium on top of Alzheimer disease, labs, UA and CXR unremarkable, no cause found, settled overnight without medication.

Daughter says she has been back to her usual self since she came home - calm, sleeping, eating, no shouting. No fever, cough, urinary symptoms, constipation or pain that the daughter has noticed. Taking all meds; sertraline in the pack. ED list showed hydrochlorothiazide and missed sertraline - both stale; our list is correct.

Exam: afebrile, vitals as charted, weight 57.5. Calm, pleasant, oriented to person. Heart: soft SEM. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Nonfocal.

A/P:
1. Delirium - resolved; back at baseline. Daughter given signs to watch for.
2. Alzheimer disease, MDD with psychotic features - stable on sertraline 50.
3. DM, HTN, HLD - routine visit in May.
